observations.what_it_proves: P3066 is an active 1,864 MW Load request in Clearwater County with POI 38-Caroline; developer is not exposed.
P3066 appears as a 1,864 MW Data Load in the Caroline planning area at Stage 2 / assessment, with ISD under review.
The Caroline planning area has 1,864 DTS MW across 2 projects and lists P3066 as Data Load; substation/POI context is not a facility coordinate.

The current Connection Project List shows P3066 Leedale Data Load at 1,864 MW DTS, Data Load, Caroline planning area, Stage 2 Assessment, with ISD under review. GridLens states DTS/STS are contract-capacity figures, not current site demand.
A secondary tracker classifies P3066 as a proposed data center and retains 1,864 MW, but leaves the developer blank. This is classification corroboration, not entity proof.

P3066 is included in the Caroline planning-area project set associated with 581S/Ricinus; the page identifies 581S as a 138 kV Caroline/ Clearwater County facility with DLS context 35-8-W5. This is planning-area infrastructure context, not a definitive POI or parcel assignment.
The current list retains P3066 at 1,864 MW DTS, Data Load, Caroline, Stage 2 assessment, with ISD under review. The site explicitly warns DTS/STS are contract-capacity changes, not current demand.
The public tracker retains P3066 as proposed, 1,864 MW, Clearwater County, with AESO as the grid operator and no named developer/operator/owner exposed.

do_not_infer: Clearwater County is not a parcel
POI 38-Caroline is not the facility address
1,864 MW is not measured electricity or IT load
secondary data-center classification is not developer/owner proof

observations.what_it_proves: P3198 is listed as an 1,800 MW Data Load in Fort Saskatchewan, Stage 1 / assessment, ISD under review.
P3198 appears in the Fort Saskatchewan planning area alongside the 439S substation context; this does not establish a parcel.
P3198 is one of 45 current Alberta data-load projects and was detected as newly listed in August 2026.
The current Connection Project List shows P3198 Lynx Data Load at 1,800 MW DTS, Data Load, Fort Saskatchewan planning area, Stage 1 Assessment, with ISD under review.
P3198 appears within the Fort Saskatchewan planning-area context associated with Opal 439S; the page does not establish that 439S is the facility's service point.
P3198 also appears in a Fort Saskatchewan planning-area record associated with Westwood 422S; this does not establish a parcel or definitive service assignment.

P3198 is included in the Fort Saskatchewan planning-area project set shown with 402S/Shell AOSP; the page gives 402S as 138 kV and DLS context 56-21-W4. This does not establish that 402S is the P3198 point of service.

P3198 is included in the Fort Saskatchewan planning-area project set shown with 439S/Opal; 439S is identified as a 138 kV facility in Sturgeon County with DLS context 56-22-W4. This is context, not definitive service assignment.

P3198 is also included in the Fort Saskatchewan planning-area project set shown with 430S/Ursus. The page lists nearby substations and other industrial/data-load projects, but does not expose a parcel-level P3198 assignment.
P3198 is retained as an AESO data-center load record, but the public summary leaves the physical site and developer fields unresolved.

do_not_infer: Fort Saskatchewan planning area is not a parcel
substation association is not physical-site identity
Data Load is not measured electricity
no developer name is not evidence of concealment

observations.what_it_proves: P2958 is a proposed Fort Saskatchewan load facility request associated with the Ft. Sask. Path2Zero materials; the project is explicitly modeled as Industrial in the AESO study scope.
P2958 is an active 320 MW Load request in Strathcona County with POI 33-Fort Saskatchewan; the public page does not expose the developer.
P2958 is currently shown as a 320 MW Industrial Load in the Fort Saskatchewan planning area at Stage 2 Assessment with ISD under review.

do_not_infer: industrial load does not imply compute
connection-study load does not equal measured operating demand

observations.what_it_proves: Dow Chemical Canada ULC submitted the request; requested new-facility DTS capacity is 231 MW and the study's project component is identified as Industrial. The document also describes existing Dow Fort Saskatchewan load and waste-heat generation context.
P2614 is listed as a 231 MW Industrial Load in Fort Saskatchewan, Stage 4 / AUC Applications, with ISD 2027-09-01.

observations.source: AESO Fort Saskatchewan Path2Zero Expansion Connection
observations.what_it_proves: AESO identifies Dow Chemical Canada ULC as the applicant for the Fort Saskatchewan Path2Zero Expansion and describes a proposed connection solution using two 240 kV lines to Lamoureux 71S plus substation modifications.

The proposed-transmission map places the project in the Fort Saskatchewan area and labels the Dow Chemical Fort Saskatchewan 166S/Main Site BLK 80 1199S context; this is infrastructure context, not measured load.

The February 28, 2025 service-proposal estimate identifies DOW Fort Saskatchewan Load as AESO project P2614/D.0886 and gives an estimated 2026 in-service date; this is project documentation, not proof of energization.

do_not_infer: project-study capacity is not measured operating demand
industrial classification does not imply compute
transmission modifications are not evidence of current load

semantics: Source observations are claim-scoped. Secondary trackers remain secondary and do not overwrite publisher-origin fields. Official AESO study documents establish project-study facts, not independent proof of current operation.

observations.what_it_proves: The current public synthesis reports the Wild Rose Power Hub planning area at about 479 acres, identifies SW/SE/NE 09-23-27W04, and describes a two-stage 1,300 MW AESO request. It explicitly distinguishes developer projections from verified public-record facts.

current_source_audit.methodology: Live public-source review of all five strict pilot cases. Secondary trackers are retained as corroboration and do not overwrite publisher-origin classifications.
findings: P3066 remains a large public Data Load; no checked source resolved developer or facility parcel.
P3198 remains a large public Data Load; planning/substation context exists but no checked source established developer or definitive parcel/service assignment.
P3108 has official planning identity/parcel context plus retained remote-sensing observations; operation, energization and measured demand remain unproven.
P2958 remains an explicit Industrial Load control; no compute interpretation is assigned.
P2614 has official applicant and proposed-transmission linkage to Dow Chemical Canada ULC; industrial-control status is retained.
New September 27 queue/substation checks add planning-area infrastructure context for P3066 and P3198 without converting that context into false parcel or POI certainty.
